notes: 2 stone lines; (2) printed before wos. Assembled from the table: A right column 'tewiseti :', A left column 'apote : yebye : tiso :'; section B row empty; C right column '(2)wos : pileqeteli :', C left column 'nlw : berkelo :', then 'end'. Description p. 45 (n64): the first two characters in each line are worn but can easily be restored; nearly identical with the inscription in the Colonnade. English (p. 51, n70): 'The adoration made by the envoy piously unto Isis in Philae.' Griffith: te-wisti = demotic t-wste 'the salutation, obeisance'; apote = 'envoy' (also in 95, 123, all neatly executed, perhaps by one person); the group ending -so (here tiso) means something like 'of, done by'; nlw + berkelo render 'piously (before)'. No query marks or sic in this row. Checked at 2.5-3.5x: the 3-shaped sign of tiso is the closed s of wos (not m or ẖ); berkelo has k (flat Z top, as in ksbñ), not p. ' | ' separates the parts of the text taken from the successive sections (A to E) of Griffith's Table of Seven Graffiti of Philae (p. 50); within a section the right-hand column is read before the left-hand one, and a section printed on several lines is joined; (n) is his superscript stone-line number, kept where printed; [x] his restoration; [.] a lost sign; [...] his dots.

notes: 11 stone lines; (2)-(11) printed. Assembled from the table: A right 'tewiseti :', A left 'ḫbḫeñ : (2)qorise : qoreñ (3)blyeso :'; B 'pelmos ato(4)lit yetmdelo :'; C right 'wos : pile(5)qeteli :', C left 'wos : tebweteli : (6)nlw : berwi :'; D printed on three lines: 'perite wost (7)qoreñ wost : yetmdelo :', '(8)mey : mebrse : penylito', and '(9)mdek : pileqetelo :' (right) + 'mde : (10)pẖrsetelo :' (left); E 'ksbñ : wos : (11)sebto :'. Griffith's queries (? over the sign): l of blyeso; y of mey; y of penylito; p of pẖrsetelo. Description pp. 47-48 (n66-n67): the stone has deteriorated; much of it, especially the lower lines, is very obscure, lightly engraved or worn down, but parallel passages help the reading greatly and few signs remain uncertain. English (pp. 51-52, n70-n71): 'The adoration made by (?) the khabkhen of the king, and qeren, the kin of the strategus of the water, remaining (?) before Isis in Philae and Isis in Tebawe; kin of the Agent of Isis and qeren of Isis, mey-mebaras of penay(l), mazek in Philae, maze in Pachoras, belonging to the kashbam of Isis' (cf. 111/15). Griffith: perite wost qoreñ wost = demotic p qrny n 3S p rt n 3S, 'the qeren of Isis, the Agent of Isis'; pelmos = strategus; pẖrse-telo (122/10) a place-name, Pachoras, probably modern Faras; 122 and 123 end in the same three words. Printed only in the Table of Seven Graffiti of Philae (p. 50), assembled from its rows in section order: A (the right column tewiseti, then the left part), B, C (right part, then left part), E; section D has no row for 123 (its lines numbered 7 to 10 belong to 122). Assembled from the table: A right 'tewiseti :', A left 'a[s]y ye[bye] (2)t[iso]'; B '. . . . . qo' (the dots stand right of qo, so they are read first); C right 'wos', C left 'nlw', then 'end'. Griffith's queries (? over the sign): the restored s and the y of a[s]y, the e of ye[bye], the t of t[iso]; bye and iso are his restorations (after the parallel yebye : tiso of 121). Notes pp. 48-49 (n67-n68): much worn and injured, many round pittings, so no dividers marked except after the first word; the right-hand end of l. 2 is cut to pieces; l. 1: 'It seems hardly possible to read apote here. Nothing is recognizable after ye, and perhaps nothing more was engraved'; l. 2: traces in the first half, possibly left blank, 'at the beginning, however, t is fairly clear'; qo is followed by a space before the cross; of two cuttings at the top of the cross the second might be the remains of a sign, the first is not a Meroitic letter; no third line. The gate is late (perhaps Diocletian's fortifications), so the text is probably 4th century AD or later, the most northerly Meroitic inscription. English (p. 51): 'The adoration made by (?) the .... .... unto Isis.' Griffith: nlw ('before' ?) is used alone here. The 3-shaped restored sign of a[s]y and t[iso] is the closed s of wos. notes: Griffith says ends of ten lines; his superscript numbers 2 to 11 are printed, each before the lost beginning of its line (the left half survives, so every line keeps only its end). Here ' | ' marks his six printed rows, which run on from line to line; the stone lines are the (n) marks. Griffith: the first three lines held the names and titles of Natakamani (ntkmn[i]), Amanitere (mnitor[e]) and [A?]rakakharer ([a]rkḫror); his footnote: the loss of the first letter of the prince's name and the absence of i after r leave some doubt about the identification. ll. 5-9: 'The well-known title kharpkhen seems probable' (ḫrp(5)[ḫeñ] and [ḫr]pḫe(10)[ñ]); yeqe 'occurs on the Isis from Napata, no. 75'; qedi 'is a title'; l. 8 'probably ended with a proper name' (debñqo). His queries ('?' printed over the sign): q of qedi; both restored signs of [ḫr]pḫe; the divider after mkli. His restorations: [i], [e], [:], [a], [ḫeñ], [ḫr], [ñ]. Checked at 4x: every 3-sign here is the narrow smooth m (ntkmni, mnitore, mñ, mkli); k has the angular Z top (ntkmni, arkḫror, mkli), p the rounded top (ḫrp, pḫe); in yeqe the q is the single q sign (stroke + ɔ), not o + q; to in mnitor[e] is the barred hook with the dot below. Space kept as printed in 'qedi te'.
